title: Climate Change (Management) Act 2015, as consolidated by the CCDA with the 2021 and 2023 amendments
citation: Climate Change (Management) Act 2015 (the CCDA file leaves the Act number blank), with the Climate Change (Management) Amendment Acts 2021 and 2023 as named in the file footnotes
evidence: Enacting words in the CCDA consolidated PDF: "MADE by the National Parliament to come into operation in accordance with a notice in the National Gazette by the Head of State, acting with, and in accordance with, the advice of the Minister." No official page opened states the gazette notice date.
notes: Climate framework Act: national sector targets and a biennial national emissions calculation (ss. 53-55 per the earlier register read), the Papua New Guinea National Registry (s. 78A, 2021 amendment), the CCDA carbon market permit process and fees (Schedules 3 and 4, 2023 amendment). Link only because no official page states the first in-force date or the in-force dates of the 2021 and 2023 amendments, and the CCDA consolidation (https://ccda.gov.pg/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Climate-Change-Management-Act-2015_consolidated.pdf, 72 pages, text layer, no dates inside) is a single undated version, so there is no date to put on a record. Row PG-CCDA-CONSOLIDATED passes on statute, so the text could be stored once a gazette date is read. The old register URL https://www.parliament.gov.pg/uploads/acts/15A-19.pdf answers 404 and the Parliament site lists no Act. The amending Acts as passed were not found on the CCDA, Parliament or CEPA sites. Implemented by pg-ndc-regulation-2022 and pg-carbon-markets-regulation-2025. English only; no Tok Pisin or Hiri Motu text found.

title: Climate Change (Management) (Nationally Determined Contribution) Regulation 2022
citation: Statutory Instrument No. [blank] of 2022, made under the Climate Change (Management) Act 2015
evidence: Signed page of the Statutory Instrument: "MADE this Monday, 25th day of April, 2022." (Governor-General signature; handwritten date read from the page image, OCR text garbles it). The Regulation has no commencement clause.
notes: Designates the CCDA, sets up a Technical Advisory Committee, requires regulated sectors to collect and report greenhouse gas data (s. 19) and makes failure to do so an offence (s. 21: K10,000 for a natural person, K100,000 for a body corporate). in_force is the date the Regulation was made, because it has no commencement clause and no official page states a later date (lookup policy for an instrument without a commencement clause). Stored 2026-11-03, one record, English. The record text is uncorrected OCR output (tesseract 5.3.4, eng, 300 dpi) of a scanned official PDF with no text layer; it contains OCR errors, including in handwritten dates, which were not corrected by hand. English is the language of legislation in Papua New Guinea; Tok Pisin and Hiri Motu are official languages but no Tok Pisin or Hiri Motu text of this instrument was found on the publisher's site, and Tok Pisin has no ISO 639-1 code, so none is stored. No government English translation is needed (the text is English).

title: Climate Change (Management) (Carbon Markets) Regulation 2025
citation: Statutory Instrument No. [blank] of 2025, made under the Climate Change (Management) Act 2015

title: SCPNG Green Bond Guidelines 2026/001
citation: Securities Commission of Papua New Guinea, Guidelines 2026/001, Gazette No. G578 of 2026
evidence: Cover page: "ISSUED: 10th JUNE 2026"; every page: "Issued by publication in the National Gazette under Gazette No. G578 Of 2026"; instrument: "with effect on and from the date of publication of this instrument in the National Gazette". The gazette publication date itself is not on the SCPNG page, so the issue date is used.
notes: Issuer-facing guidance for bonds labelled Green: use of proceeds, process, management of proceeds and reporting. The Guidelines say they are not mandatory in themselves and bind only when incorporated by reference (sovereign framework or exchange listing rules). Gazette notice signed by the Acting CEO. title: Commercial Advertisement (Protection of the Public) Act 1976 (Chapter 352)
citation: Commercial Advertisement (Protection of the Public) Act 1976 (Ch. 352)
evidence: No official page opened states a commencement date: the ICCC PDF (https://iccc.gov.pg/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Commercial-Advertisement-Protection-of-the-Public-Act-1976.pdf) reads "Certified on: / /20 ." with the date blank.
notes: s. 3: a person who publishes an "unfair statement" in a commercial advertisement commits an offence (fine up to K1,000); "unfair statement" is one "untrue or inaccurate or misleading or misrepresentative or unreasonable in describing the size, quality, quantity or nature of goods or services". It is the only misleading-advertising provision found. The Independent Consumer and Competition Commission Act 2002 (No. 6 of 2002, certified 26/4/2002, https://iccc.gov.pg/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Independent-Consumer-and-Competition-Commission-Act-2002.pdf) was read in full for this: it has no misleading or deceptive conduct prohibition (Part 7 covers consumer policy, product safety, product information standards and recalls), so it is not in scope as a green-claims umbrella. Link only because no commencement date is stated on any official page. Row PG-ICCC-CONSOLIDATED passes on statute. English only.
